title: Oak-Poached Mahi-Mahi with Mild Ancho-Cocoa Gravy
description: A little cocoa and smooth pumpkin seed paste round out a mild ancho gravy for oak-poached mahi-mahi.

ingredients.name: skinless mahi-mahi fillet
ingredients.note: Weight after skin and pin bones are removed. Divide into two even portions about 3/4 to 1 inch thick. Fully thaw before cooking.

ingredients.name: low-sodium chicken broth
ingredients.note: Choose unsalted plain meat-and-water broth without a vegetable blend.

ingredients.name: smooth unsalted pumpkin seed paste
ingredients.note: Pure pumpkin seeds, ground completely smooth.

steps.title: Heat the Traeger
steps.text: Load the Traeger Silverton 610 with oak wood pellets. Preheat with the lid closed to 300°F, allowing about 15 minutes.

steps.title: Infuse the poaching broth
steps.text: Bring {broth} and {garlic} to a simmer in the small Dutch oven on the stovetop. Place the pot uncovered on the smoker grate under the closed smoker lid for 10–12 minutes.

steps.title: Make the cocoa paste
steps.text: In the cool HexClad, whisk {ancho}, {cocoa}, {pepita} and {maple} with a splash of the smoky broth until the paste is smooth. Keep it on the stovetop for finishing.

steps.title: Cover the mahi-mahi
steps.text: Lay {fish} in the remaining hot broth on the Traeger and spoon some broth over the tops. Fit the pot lid immediately as the wrap from the start.

steps.title: Poach to the pull point
steps.text: Cook at 300°F and check from 7 minutes. Pull each portion at 135°F in its thickest center, typically after 9–18 minutes.

steps.title: Rest under cover
steps.text: Transfer the fish to a warm plate. Cover and rest for 3 minutes while finishing the gravy.

steps.title: Build the ancho gravy
steps.text: Whisk the poaching broth into the cocoa paste in stages. Bring the sauce to a full boil for 1 minute, scraping the sides of the pan.

steps.title: Bind the sauce
steps.text: Bring the sauce to a simmer. Whisk in the freshly stirred slurry and let it bubble gently for 1 minute, stirring until it coats the back of a spoon.

steps.title: Check carryover and doneness
steps.text: After resting, check each thickest center for about 140°F. Open a natural seam with a fork. The center should be opaque and separate easily into flakes. If either cue is unclear or the center is below 140°F, finish covered in hot sauce in the HexClad over low heat to a measured 145°F, checking every minute.

steps.title: Spoon into bowls
steps.text: Lay a piece of fish in each bowl. Spoon the ancho gravy over the surface and between the flakes. Serve with the rest of the gravy around the fish.

notes: Sauce yield: About 1 1/2 cups for two. Make ahead: Blend the cocoa, pumpkin seed paste, maple and ancho together a day ahead and refrigerate. Loosen with warm broth when ready to cook. Refrigerate shallow portions within 2 hours, or within 1 hour outdoors above 90°F. Use refrigerated leftovers within 3 days. Freezer-Friendly Verdict: Yes. The pumpkin seed paste helps the reheated sauce cling to the fish. Freeze covered portions for up to 1 month. Fridge reheat: Warm a portion covered in its sauce over medium-low heat in the HexClad. Add a little water if it has thickened in storage. Check from 5 minutes and heat to 165°F at the coldest center. Freezer reheat: If frozen, thaw the covered portion in the refrigerator overnight, then follow the fridge method. Option A uses a small amount of mild ancho and cocoa. For gentler Option B, leave out both and use sweet paprika with a little extra pumpkin seed paste. Both versions are dairy-free. Estimated nutrition per serving (1/2 of recipe): 199 kcal, 30.3 g protein, 7.8 g total carbohydrate, 5.0 g fat, 0.9 g fiber, 154 mg sodium. Includes both the fish and its full share of sauce and any rice or potatoes listed. Sodium varies with the broth.
